# Almanac of Guitar Voice Leading, Vol. 3 — Statement of Outputs

## Overview

Mick Goodrick's *Almanac of Guitar Voice Leading, Volume 3* is the culminating installment of a three-part method for systematic guitar voice-leading. Where the first two volumes established foundational voicing types and introduced a working vocabulary of harmonic motion, this volume completes the taxonomy, names what was previously nameless, and turns classification into application. The book's architecture is deliberately cumulative: it opens with terminological groundwork (Chapter 1), builds a closed and finite classification system across Chapters 2 through 9, and then pivots in Chapters 10 through 12 to practical voice-leading procedure.

The spine of the method is the M-Lode framework, a comprehensive taxonomy of guitar chord voicings organized into paired 3-part and 4-part families distinguished by interval content. This volume adds the three chord categories needed to close the system: 7th chords with no 3rd, 7th chords with no 5th, and 3-part spread clusters. The characteristic procedural move throughout is derivation — generating smaller structures by systematically omitting voices from larger parent chords — and Chapters 5 through 9 each demonstrate one derivation pathway through the families.

The book's governing aesthetic claim, stated explicitly in Chapter 12, is that excellent voice-leading treats melody and harmony as structural equals. Every analytical tool introduced — the M.S.R.P. sequence, the GDVL/SCVL distinction, the six generic voice-leading patterns, the Grip-Slipping technique — serves this principle. The author identifies Chapter 11, presenting twenty foundational 3-part chord types (which expand to one hundred twenty distinct voicings when close and spread inversions are counted), as the most important chapter in the volume.

## Systems

### The Real, Compleat M-Lode Taxonomy System

The M-Lode system is a closed, finite classification of all guitar chord voicings, organized into families defined by interval content and paired by structural density. Each 3-part family maps to exactly one 4-part counterpart: Triads pair with 7th Chords; 7th-no-3rd pairs with TBN I; 7th-no-5th pairs with TBN II; 3-Part 4ths pair with 4-Part 4ths; and 3-Part Spread Clusters pair with 4-Part Spread Clusters. The system is finite because the 4-Part Spread Clusters supply the previously-missing link. Interval omissions are structurally permitted only within three specific 3-part families (triads, 3-part 4ths, spread clusters), while the four families with the most even interval distribution (7th no-3rd, 7th no-5th, TBN I, TBN II) behave consistently across density levels.

Traversal: **Family Pairing Navigation** (`FamilyCoherence`, ch3) and **Four-Family Even-Distribution Symmetry** (`SymmetryMovement`, ch4). Modification: **Interval Omission Restricted to Three Families** (`OmissionAllow`, ch4), **Spread Cluster Literal-Pitch Naming Rule** (`_pending:literal-pitch-naming`, ch3), **Sus4 Notation Rule for Stacked-Fourth Chords** (`_pending:chord-naming-convention`, ch2).

### Voice-Reduction Derivation System

The derivation system is the method's central generative procedure: smaller chord structures are produced by systematically omitting one voice from a larger parent chord. The full toolkit comprises Drop 2, Drop 3, Drop 2&3, Drop 2&4, and Double Drop 2 Drop 3 procedures applied across root positions and inversions of each 4-part parent family. The key symmetry principle is that each 3-part chord type appears inside exactly four different 4-part families, creating a cross-family substitution lattice with direct reharmonization implications.

Traversal: **Four-Family Symmetry Reharmonization** (`SubstitutionExpand`, ch5). Modification: **Voice Omission Derivation Procedure** (`OmissionAllow`, ch5), **Density Floor: Three-Voice Minimum** (`DensityFloor`, ch11), **Grip-Slipping Inversion Cycle** (`_pending:inversion-cycling`, ch12).

### Diatonic and Chromatic Voice-Leading Application System

This system governs how M-Lode voicings are moved through harmonic progressions. It operates over five parent scales (C Major, C Melodic Minor, C Harmonic Minor, C Harmonic Major, C Hungarian Minor) and distinguishes Generic Diatonic Voice-Leading (GDVL) from Specific Chromatic Voice-Leading (SCVL). Voice-leading patterns are analyzed via abstract A-B-C labels that separate intervallic motion from functional motion (tracked by the M.S.R.P. sequence). Six possible generic voice-leading patterns exist; prior volumes used only three.

Traversal: **Diatonic Scale Transposition Expectation** (`VoiceMotion`, ch10/ch12), **Generic Voice-Leading Pattern Selection (6-Pattern Space)** (`VoiceMotion`, ch10), **Intervallic vs. Functional Motion Analysis** (`VoiceMotion`, ch10), **Melody-Harmony Equality Aesthetic Rule** (`_pending:aesthetic-balance`, ch12). Modification: **GDVL-to-SCVL Mode Switch** (`_pending:vl-mode-switch`, ch12), **Duet Texture with Passing Tones** (`TextureCycle`, ch10), **Harmonic Major b6 Substitution** (`SubstitutionExpand`, ch12), **Hungarian Minor #4 Substitution** (`SubstitutionExpand`, ch12).
